answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. The way a cedar roots the soil, a summit returns each spring, and a voyage reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
